events.title: The death of Pope Julius III
events.shortBlurb: The cardinal who had opened the Council of Trent became its restorer as pope, and died as England returned to Rome…
body: Giovanni Maria del Monte had stood at the Council of Trent's cradle: made a cardinal by Paul III in 1536, he was first of the three legates who opened the council on 13 December 1545. Elected pope on 7 February 1550 after ten weeks of conclave, against the emperor's wishes, he took the name Julius III.

He kept the jubilee of 1550, confirmed the young Society of Jesus by Exposcit debitum, and founded the Collegium Germanicum in 1552 to form priests for the embattled German Church. At the emperor's urging he called the fathers back to Trent in May 1551, where they defined the doctrine of the Eucharist, penance, and anointing — until war scattered them again within a year.

His eyes reached also to England: when Mary Tudor came to the throne he sent Cardinal Pole home as legate, and in November 1554 the realm was reconciled to Rome. Worn by gout, Julius died at Rome on 23 March 1555; his Villa Giulia still witnesses the gentler side of his reign.
